pilot.summary: Game one of four at Alex's house in Orinda, three-player with Alex and Stuart. I mulliganed into a hand that looked strong and was structurally dead — clean lands, one-drop instants and sorceries, Crimson Wisps, Storm-Kiln Artist, and zero goblins — so the copy half of the engine had nothing to target and the deck fizzled. I should have shipped it. No changes to the deck; a bad keep, not a deck problem.

Game one of three at Oliver's, five-player with Oliver, Tom, Alex and Ryan. I kept three basics, a utility land and Krenko, Mob Boss — land and a payoff, but no small goblins, and the instants and sorceries in hand were all expensive, so the cantrip half never turned over. Three of the five decks were mono-red; Oliver killed the table on turn five off Krenko tokens and pings. Loss, and the same lesson as the first night: goblin presence gates the mulligan.

read.what_it_does: Across both logged games the deck never got to do its thing, and the reason was the same twice: no cheap goblin bodies to multiply through (001, 002). Game 001 had the whole copy-and-storm half in hand — cantrips, Crimson Wisps, Storm-Kiln Artist — and nothing to target. Game 002 had land and Krenko, Mob Boss and again no small goblins, with the instants and sorceries all expensive enough that the cantrip half never turned over.
read.how_it_plays: The record does not yet show the deck switched on. Both logged games are losses where it sat holding half an engine (001, 002). In the five-player game it was not the fastest red deck at the table — three mono-red decks, and Oliver killed the pod on turn five off Krenko tokens and pings while this deck was still looking for a goblin (002). In the three-player game it stalled out instead (001). Two games is not enough to say how it behaves when it does assemble; nothing in the log has seen that yet.
mindful_of: Goblin presence gates the mulligan, not cantrip density. Both keeps read as strong hands and neither had a goblin in it (001, 002).
Cantrips plus a copy engine with no body to target is a dead hand. Crimson Wisps and Storm-Kiln Artist did nothing all game (001).
Land plus a payoff is not a keep either. Krenko, Mob Boss with no small goblins, and only expensive spells behind it, left the cheap half of the deck offline (002).
In a red-heavy pod this deck is not the one that closes first. One game says so — Oliver's Krenko ended the table on turn five (002) — so treat it as a single observation, not a rule.
Sean called both losses a keep problem rather than a deck problem (001, 002). Worth holding that read lightly until a game is logged where the hand had goblins in it.
read.what_changed: Nothing has changed. The deck is on one version, precon as printed, sleeved at v1.0.0, and both games were played on it (001, 002). Sean explicitly made no changes after either loss (001, 002). That is not evidence the list is right — only that no logged game has argued against it yet.
